title: Telemetry
description: One reading emitted by a device. Envelope is generic on purpose; `readings` keys are stack-specific. The depot-node stack emits temp_c, rh_pct, pressure_hpa, gas_ohms, temp_c_xcheck, rh_pct_xcheck, mq2_mv, mq2_rs_r0, voc_index, voc_bme and voc_mq2. Any key may be absent or null: the device omits what it could not measure rather than substituting a plausible value.

device_id.description: Stable per-device identifier. Use the MCU serial, not an index.

node_id.description: Which physical location this device is reporting for (see depot.schema.json). Devices are swappable; bins are not. Null for devices not bound to a location.

country.description: ISO-2 of the point of interest this device is reporting from - the depot where supplies flow in and out, i.e. the graph's `country:` node it sits under. Set on the device (DEPOT_COUNTRY in config.h) and carried on every reading, so a node physically moved to another depot re-homes itself without anyone editing the API's seed. Depots are local to a country, not global: the UI lists this bin under this country and under no other. Null = the seed's country stands.

ts.description: UTC, RFC3339. Device clocks drift - the service may overwrite this with receipt time. OPTIONAL. The m5stack node deliberately omits it — an ESP32 has no RTC and its clock drifts, so the API stamps receipt time unless DEPOT_TRUST_DEVICE_TS=1. replay.py does send it, which is what makes the 24h MKT window real. Was listed as required until Sun 00:20, which made every real device payload contract-invalid.

seq.description: Monotonic counter. Lets the service detect dropped packets.

readings.description: Sensor payload. Keys are stack-specific; keep them flat and numeric.
